source.title: EIS VI: Critiques of Mechanistic Interpretability Work in AI Safety

record.tranche_reason: The author argues that the IOI circuit's explanatory scope is restricted to the selected sentence set, and reports checking GPT-2-small on one more complex IOI example.
record.gate_note: The post cites Wang et al.'s ablation result, but that is a result from another work and is not recorded as a row. The post does not itself ablate or patch the circuit, or measure its head classes.
record.test_reason: A critique post. It argues that the IOI circuit's algorithm (find names, remove duplicates, output the rest) covers only a restricted sentence set, not general IOI. Its only original evidence is one manually checked prompt where GPT-2 small answers correctly. It does no ablation, patching or head analysis, so it gives no result on whether the circuit or its head classes handle that prompt. The bearing on V1, V5 and V6 is argument only; no measured result can carry a verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author argues the IOI task was cherrypicked: the circuit explains IOI only on a restricted template set, leaving general IOI unexplained. He suggests the circuit may be a 'frivolous' subnetwork akin to Ramanujan et al.'s pruning-found subnetworks. He credits Wang et al.'s hierarchical approach and ablation tests, and notes (citing them) that ablation left some performance unexplained.
record.recipe_differences: The post checks one alternate prompt by observing the model's completion; it does not reproduce the original circuit discovery or intervention methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The post highlights a difference between the selected IOI sentence set and a more complex sentence involving additional names and context, but does not systematically compare prompt conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 small correctly completes one IOI-style prompt that the duplicate-removal heuristic would get wrong (answer Charlie, not Alice).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2 small solves some IOI prompts that the published circuit's algorithm would not solve, implying other mechanisms exist (single example, untested mechanistically).

record.problems: The post reports only one manually checked example, with no systematic prompt sample, quantitative performance measure, uncertainty estimate, or circuit intervention.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. The post's discussion of Wang et al.'s circuit and ablation findings refers to cited work rather than new results from this post.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, the 7 classes, faithfulness, completeness, minimality: none measured. Only argued to be scope-limited to the chosen templates.
Backup name-mover heads and self-repair not tested.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints and task reuse not tested.
No alternative circuit-finding methods, ablations or metrics compared.
Argues the circuit leaves IOI outside the template set unexplained. Cites Wang et al.'s incomplete-ablation result. Reports no own measurement of ablation, metric or distribution sensitivity.
One harder prompt (three names, extra context) checked for model output only. Whether the circuit or other components carry it is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from 'tests' to 'discusses'. The post gives a specific argument against the scope of V1 and V6 (T5-style), but its only result is model output on one prompt, with no circuit intervention. So no row can carry a verdict on any version. The Wang et al. ablation finding it mentions is a cited result from the original source and is correctly not a row.

versions.untested_parts: The post argues that the circuit does not explain IOI beyond the studied sentence set, but does not test the 26 heads, their seven classes, the faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria, or circuit ablations.
Backup-head takeover and self-repair are not tested.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse for other tasks are not tested.
Other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, and metrics are not compared.
The post does not compare ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions to assess evaluation sensitivity.
It reports one different sentence example, but does not test whether the proposed circuit carries IOI across prompt variants.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: The author checked the model's completion on a more complex IOI sentence.

conditions.value: Alice reminded Bob that it was Charlie’s birthday and that Charlie wanted roller skates. So Bob gave a gift of roller skates to ___

rows.measure: Whether the model gives the correct indirect object completion
rows.value: The author states that GPT2-small gets the completion right: Charlie.
rows.note: The post presents this as an example outside the restricted sentence set analyzed by Wang et al.; it does not test which circuit produces the answer.
rows.check: Linking to none is correct. The row shows only that the model's output is correct on one prompt (single example, no baseline). It does not show which components produce the answer, so it cannot bear on V6's circuit-carries-IOI claim. State 'observed' applies only to model correctness.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
